name: Slack file upload

known_strips: JPEG trailing bytes past EOI (via re-encode)
technical_body.retrieval_gotcha: url_private_download requires the bot token; public URLs are one-shot

notes: File-bytes canonical form. PNG LSB (all channel/bit/strategy variants tested) is byte-identical; JPEG is always re-encoded; PNG private chunks pass through but named text chunks don't.

name: Slack message body paste

technical_body.api_retrieve: conversations.history — walk blocks[].rich_text_section.elements[] and read the `unicode` field on emoji nodes
known_recodes: emoji to :colon_form: in the flat .text field (VS-16 / skintone modifiers lost if consumer reads .text instead of blocks)
technical_body.retrieval_gotcha: conversations.history `.text` is (a) colon-form and (b) length-capped — do not compare against it

notes: Rendered-post canonical form. 13 of 15 text techniques survive; whitespace and invisible_ink recoded. Emoji-attached data (VS-16, skintone bits, tag sequences) rides `blocks` — only reliable when both sides walk the blocks tree.

name: Slack text snippet upload

technical_body.api_send: files.upload snippet_type=text (deprecated as of 2026-07 but working)
technical_body.retrieval_gotcha: requires the bot token; treat as an attachment fetch

notes: Raw bytes end-to-end. Strictly stronger than paste for text stego — every text technique tested survives, including whitespace and invisible_ink that recode on paste.

name: Discord file upload

technical_body.api_send: Discord REST API POST /channels/{id}/messages with multipart attachments
technical_body.canonical_layer: file-bytes (mostly — some server-side re-encode for stickers/emojis)
known_strips: reported: some EXIF stripping on large images
known_recodes: reported: WebP conversion for oversize uploads
technical_body.retrieval_gotcha: CDN URLs are ephemeral; refresh via message fetch

notes: Community-reported behavior; no ST3GG probe run yet. Treat entries in survival.json as folklore until measured.

name: Discord message body paste

known_recodes: custom emoji rendered as :name:; standard emoji preserved as codepoints

notes: Similar canonical layer to slack_paste; behavior differs in the specifics. No dedicated probe yet.

name: Telegram photo attachment (compressed)

known_recodes: JPEG re-encode at Telegram's target quality

notes: Photo-mode uploads recompress. Kills LSB; DCT-robust variants may or may not survive. Use file mode instead when payload matters.

name: Telegram file attachment (uncompressed)
notes: Send-as-file mode preserves bytes end-to-end. The happy path for image and text stego on Telegram.

name: WhatsApp photo attachment

known_recodes: aggressive JPEG re-encode with fixed Q

notes: Notoriously destructive on image bytes. LSB dies; F5/jsteg die; only spread-spectrum / DCT-robust survives (rarely, with luck). Send as document instead.

name: WhatsApp document attachment
notes: Send-as-document preserves bytes. Use this whenever an image payload has to survive WhatsApp.

name: Signal attachment
notes: Signal preserves bytes on documents; strips EXIF from images by design. Steg-friendly except for image metadata.

name: iMessage photo attachment

known_recodes: HEIC transcode on some device pairs

notes: iOS-to-iOS often preserves; cross-platform (iOS↔Android via SMS/MMS fallback) mangles.

name: Email SMTP attachment

known_strips: some mail-security gateways strip macros / active content

notes: Attachments are MIME base64. Byte-identical on retrieval for anything the security gateway doesn't touch.

name: Gmail inline image (in message body)

known_strips: inline images may be proxied through googleusercontent.com — CDN can strip metadata
known_recodes: large inline images may be re-encoded for size

notes: Inline is not the same as attached. Prefer attachment for bit-preserving delivery.

name: GitHub web UI file upload
notes: Bytes preserved end-to-end. One of the strongest steg-friendly public transports.

name: Terminal stdout + mouse-copy
notes: The user's mouse selection copies glyphs, not bytes. Zero-width / invisibles filtered by many terminals. Pipe through pbcopy / xclip / clip.exe instead.

name: OS clipboard byte-stream (pbcopy / xclip / clip.exe)
notes: Preserves bytes end-to-end. The right way to move text stego from terminal to any GUI.
